sections.title: Intake
sections.conclusion: Baseline fields and source anchors establish whether the proposal can be reviewed at all.

sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes
Requested: Fund a 12-month Governance Incentives Framework project to research, model, test, dashboard, and propose governance incentive mechanisms for Cardano.

Deliverables: Governance Incentives Framework, public dataset and dashboard, documented incentive model and formula outputs, controlled incentive pilot findings, public research and community feedback reports, at least one publication-ready research paper submitted for peer review, completed and submitted Governance Incentives Framework CIP, governance integration pathway, final financial and milestone report

Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The proposal requests ₳4,207,967 for a 12-month Governance Incentives Framework project covering research, data, modeling, community engagement, dashboarding, pilot testing, and governance integration.

Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, high materiality): The document says Cardano currently lacks a structured, data-driven framework for determining how governance contributions should be incentivized, measured, or supported over time.

Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, high materiality): The document cites early governance data showing active DReps declined in every 12-epoch period, the DRep Gini coefficient rose from 0.92 to 0.94, and 11-16 DReps represent 51% of voting power.

Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, high materiality): The document says the State of Governance research identified an incentive deficit as a major structural barrier and that one Constitutional Committee consortium retired due to lack of compensation.

Claim (governance, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The project commits to evaluate incentive mechanisms for participation quality, reward distribution, concentration risk, accountability, delegator effects, gaming risk, and budget sustainability rather than treating turnout alone as success.

Claim (governance, supported_in_proposal, medium materiality): The milestones describe seven staged work packages from discovery through final reporting, with public outputs and acceptance criteria for each stage.
missing: Independent evidence for: The document says Cardano currently lacks a structured, data-driven framework for determining how governance contributions should be incentivized, measured, or supported over time.
Independent evidence for: The team section asserts prior Cardano governance, Catalyst, research, ambassador, consulting, and project closeout experience for Seomon, Sebastian Pereira, and Cerkoryn.
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

sections.title: Treasury analysis
findings: Six-month treasury flow regime: unsustainable (basis: total inflow (tau + donations) vs enacted withdrawals)
sections.conclusion: Treasury votes require a higher bar because they consume shared ADA and create precedent.

sections.title: Risk review
sections.conclusion: Risk is not a side note; unmitigated execution or governance risk can dominate an otherwise attractive proposal.

sections.title: Counterargument pass
findings: Strongest YES: the proposal substantiates "The proposal requests ₳4,207,967 for a 12-month Governance Incentives Framework project covering research, data, modeling, community engagement, dashboarding, pilot testing, and governance integration." and clears the evidence gates.

Strongest NO: a material claim is unsupported — "The document says Cardano currently lacks a structured, data-driven framework for determining how governance contributions should be incentivized, measured, or supported over time." — so cost or precedent may outweigh the benefit.
Strongest hold: if claims cannot be tied to replayable evidence, abstaining avoids overclaiming certainty.
sections.conclusion: A defensible rationale must show the best opposing case before it reaches a vote.

sections.title: Synthesis
findings: Final vote must be derived from completed sections above, not from a prose summary.
The public rationale should name the decisive section and the strongest counterargument.
sections.conclusion: The vote is only credible if the assessment tree shows enough work for a skeptical delegator to audit.
